unit.name: Austerity, Affluence and Discontent: Britain, 1951-1979
unit.subtitle: Rationing to rock 'n' roll, Windrush to the Winter of Discontent — Britain's post-war story.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students judge a source's usefulness purely by who wrote it ('biased therefore useless'), instead of weighing content, provenance and contextual knowledge together to make a substantiated judgement.
common_misconceptions.source: WJEC Eduqas GCSE History principal moderator and examiner reports on source-evaluation questions in Component 1; AO3 descriptors in spec section 3.1.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students explain how two interpretations differ (what each says) instead of why they differ (authors, purpose, evidence used, time of writing) — and so answer the wrong question on the 10-mark Compare Interpretations item.
common_misconceptions.source: WJEC Eduqas GCSE History examiner reports on Component 1 interpretation questions.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students treat continuity, change, cause and consequence as topic labels rather than analytical lenses. They describe events instead of using the concept to weigh significance or judge change over time.
common_misconceptions.source: WJEC Eduqas GCSE History examiner reports on Component 2 Thematic Study extended responses; AO2 descriptors in spec section 3.1.

common_misconceptions.topic: Thematic change over a thousand years
common_misconceptions.misconception: Students treat the thematic study (c500 to present) as a chronological list of events rather than weighing change against continuity across the medieval, early modern and modern eras — losing the AO2 'change and continuity' marks.
common_misconceptions.source: WJEC Eduqas GCSE History examiner reports on Component 2 Thematic Study (Crime and Punishment / Health and Medicine / Warfare / Entertainment).

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students describe the named site without linking it to the wider thematic story — missing the 10% spec weighting attached to the historic environment essay.
common_misconceptions.source: Spec section 2.1 (Study of the historic environment); WJEC Eduqas GCSE History published exemplar answers.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students avoid specialist historical vocabulary (e.g. recusancy, Junkers, NEP, perestroika, Anschluss) and so cannot reach the top SPaG band, which rewards a wide range of historical terms used accurately.
common_misconceptions.source: Spec section 4.4.3 SPaG descriptors; WJEC Eduqas GCSE History examiner reports.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students answer 12-mark and 16-mark extended responses in the first person or as a diary entry rather than as a structured analytical essay, capping AO2 marks.
common_misconceptions.source: WJEC Eduqas GCSE History examiner reports flagging this as a recurring issue on extended-response questions.

student_errors_by_question_type.5 marks — Source Utility: Top-band answers integrate content, provenance and student's own contextual knowledge — not two of the three. Examiners flag responses that describe the source without judging usefulness for a specific enquiry.
student_errors_by_question_type.10 marks — Compare Interpretations: Students must focus on WHY interpretations differ (authors, purpose, sources used, time of writing) — explaining HOW they differ loses access to the top band.
student_errors_by_question_type.12 marks — Evaluate an Interpretation: Students must agree AND disagree with the interpretation using own contextual knowledge before reaching a substantiated overall judgement. Pure agreement or disagreement caps the response.
student_errors_by_question_type.16 marks — Period Essay (Component 2 Per: Top band requires substantiated overall judgement on the question (not just both sides covered). Weaker responses describe two factors without weighing them.
student_errors_by_question_type.16 marks — Thematic Change Essay (Compon: Must trace change across all three eras (medieval, early modern, modern) and weigh change against continuity. Single-era answers cap at mid-band.
student_errors_by_question_type.8 marks — Explain Significance: Top band requires significance at the time AND over time. Students who only address contemporary impact cap below top band.

topic_weighting_notes: Component 1 = 50%, Component 2 = 50%. Each component is two papers (Component 1: two 1-hour papers; Component 2: 45 mins Period Study + 1hr 15 mins Thematic Study).
AO1 = 35%, AO2 = 35%, AO3 = 15%, AO4 = 15%. Knowledge and second-order analysis carry the most weight.
Component 1 emphasises sources (AO3 12%) and interpretations (AO4 15%); Component 2 emphasises second-order concepts (AO2 27%).
The historic environment site within the Thematic Study is worth 10% of the qualification — equivalent to a full lesson's worth of revision focus per pathway.
British history must form at least 40% of assessed content; this is delivered via the British depth study (Component 1) plus the British-based thematic study (Component 2).

current_spec_changes.change: Thematic Study historic environment sites are updated for the 2026-2027 assessment cycle: Crime and Punishment = Policing in Liverpool c.1787-1900; Health and Medicine = Letchworth Garden City c.1903-present; Warfare = Royal Dockyards, Chatham c.1567-1984; Entertainment = Glastonbury Festival c.1970-present.
current_spec_changes.source: WJEC Eduqas GCSE History spec Version 5 October 2024, pp.24-31.

current_spec_changes.change: No subject-content changes for the 2016 spec across the 2026 cycle; the Version 5 (October 2024) edition only updates historic environment sites and resit rules.
current_spec_changes.source: WJEC Eduqas GCSE History spec Version 5 October 2024, summary of amendments.

current_spec_changes.change: Qualification is not available to candidates in maintained schools and colleges in Wales — those candidates take WJEC 3100QS (separate spec with mandatory Welsh history) instead.
current_spec_changes.source: WJEC Eduqas GCSE History spec Version 5 October 2024, p.1.

pedagogical_notes.note: EEF Improving Literacy in Secondary Schools recommends explicit teaching of disciplinary vocabulary — front-load second-order concepts (cause, consequence, change, continuity, significance, similarity, difference) so students deploy them confidently in extended responses.
pedagogical_notes.source: Education Endowment Foundation, Improving Literacy in Secondary Schools guidance report.

pedagogical_notes.note: EEF Metacognition and Self-Regulated Learning recommends modelling expert thinking — for source/interpretation questions, walk students through how a historian decides content vs provenance vs context, not just give them a checklist.
pedagogical_notes.source: Education Endowment Foundation, Metacognition and Self-Regulated Learning guidance report.

pedagogical_notes.note: Cambridge Assessment research on history examinations notes that comparative judgement is consistently the hardest skill at GCSE — schedule extra retrieval and worked examples on the 10-mark Compare Interpretations and 16-mark essays.
pedagogical_notes.source: Cambridge Assessment Network and Research, history specifications and reports archive.

pedagogical_notes.note: Thematic Study lessons should be sequenced to surface change/continuity across all three eras (medieval, early modern, modern) within each topic — examiner reports flag that students who learn the eras as separate blocks struggle on the 16-mark thematic essay.
pedagogical_notes.source: WJEC Eduqas GCSE History examiner reports on Component 2 Thematic Study extended responses.

pedagogical_notes.note: For each Thematic Study, the historic environment site should be taught after the broader thematic narrative is established — this lets students link site to period rather than treating it as a standalone topic.
pedagogical_notes.source: Spec section 2.1 (Study of the historic environment).

lessons_in_batch.title: Britain in the early 1950s: austerity and rationing
lessons_in_batch.description: Housing shortages, rationing into 1954, the cost of the welfare state and the early-1950s sense of decline.
spec_references: Britain in the early 1950s — Austerity and rationing; housing problems; debt; nationalised industries; cost of welfare budget; industrial decline
lessons_in_batch.adaptation_notes: No equivalent in existing free-tier History — fresh.

lessons_in_batch.title: The end of austerity: 'never had it so good'
lessons_in_batch.description: Town planning, motorway investment, the Beeching axe, Macmillan's affluence and Wilson's white heat of technology.
spec_references: The end of austerity — Town planning; wage rises and tax cuts; Macmillan- 'never had it so good'; Wilson- 'white heat'; motorway investment; the Beeching axe; comprehensive education

lessons_in_batch.title: Popular entertainment and fashion: from teddy boys to punk
lessons_in_batch.description: Rock 'n' roll, the impact of TV, mini-skirts and Mods vs Rockers — and how American culture reshaped British youth.
spec_references: Popular entertainment and fashion — Changing musical styles; listening to music; popular groups and artists; impact of TV; American culture; fashion – teddy boys, mini-skirts, Mods, Rockers, hippies and punk
lessons_in_batch.adaptation_notes: Fresh — cultural content not in AQA equivalents.

lessons_in_batch.title: Changing lives of women, 1951-1979
lessons_in_batch.description: Labour-saving devices, the pill, the 1967 Abortion Act, the 1970 Equal Pay Act and the rise of women's liberation.
spec_references: Changing lives of women — Labour-saving devices; family, marriage, divorce and abortion; education and employment; women's rights; impact of the pill; equal opportunities; women's liberation
lessons_in_batch.adaptation_notes: AQA Power and the People covers women's rights post-1945 — adapt and add domestic/cultural angles. ~50% transfer.

lessons_in_batch.title: Changing attitudes to authority: the permissive society
lessons_in_batch.description: Profumo, the legalisation of homosexuality, abolition of the death penalty, CND and the student protests of 1968.
spec_references: Changing attitudes to authority — Permissive society; legalising homosexuality; drugs; abolition of the death penalty; Profumo Scandal; CND; student protest in 1968

lessons_in_batch.title: Immigration: Windrush, race riots and Enoch Powell
lessons_in_batch.description: Caribbean migration, the 1958 Notting Hill riots, Enoch Powell's 1968 speech and the Race Relations Acts.
spec_references: Immigration — Reasons for migration; British Nationality Acts 1948-65; Caribbean immigration - Windrush; race riots; Notting Hill 1958; Enoch Powell; right wing groups; race relations legislation
lessons_in_batch.adaptation_notes: AQA Migration covers Windrush and post-war migration in detail — ~80% transferable. Adapt to Eduqas British depth-study framing.

lessons_in_batch.title: Political and economic problems of the 1970s
lessons_in_batch.description: Heath, the miners and the three-day week, the Winter of Discontent and Thatcher's 1979 victory.
spec_references: Political and economic problems — Industrial decline; Heath, the miners and the three day week; the Winter of Discontent and the 1979 General Election
lessons_in_batch.adaptation_notes: AQA Power and the People touches on 1970s briefly — needs deeper treatment for Eduqas. ~50% transfer.

lessons_in_batch.title: Civil unrest in Northern Ireland
lessons_in_batch.description: Bloody Sunday, internment, IRA bombing campaigns on the mainland and how the Troubles reshaped British politics.
spec_references: Political and economic problems — civil unrest in Northern Ireland; Bloody Sunday and internment; IRA bombing campaign
lessons_in_batch.adaptation_notes: Fresh — not covered in detail in any existing free-tier History unit.

lessons_in_batch.title: Sources and interpretations: how 1951-79 has been remembered
lessons_in_batch.description: How the post-war consensus, Thatcherite hindsight and oral history have shaped competing readings of this period.

lessons_in_batch.title: Exam technique and synthesis
lessons_in_batch.description: Practise the source utility, interpretations and essay questions on austerity, affluence and discontent.
